summary:
We built Mars Base, a free browser game where kids aged 7–12 run a Mars outpost for 8 sols. Players collect supplies, build a greenhouse, rover garage and storm bunker, grow food, and keep energy, water and food above zero. Seven guided chapters show one goal at a time, with an arrow on the map.

It answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning real mission trade-offs into play: saving power in a dust storm slows the crops, and the closest shelter from a solar storm costs energy while the free one is far away. Real NASA data changes the rules: DONKI space weather sets how much time players have to find shelter, and InSight Mars weather makes cold nights cost extra food.

It matters because kids usually see how missions end, not the choices behind them. In 20–28 minutes, with no install or account, they learn that every decision has a cost, that NASA data shapes real missions, and they finish with a Junior Astronaut certificate.
